source.text: ወአልዐልኩ፡ እደየ፡ በጽድቅ፡ ወባረክዎ፡ ለቅዱስ፡ ወለዓቢይ፡ ወነገርኩ፡ በመንፈስ፡ አፉየ፡ ወ*በልሳነ፡ ሥጋ፡ *እንተ፡ ገብረ፡ አምላክ፡ ለውሉደ፡ ሥጋ፡ ሰብእ፡ *ከመ፡ ይትናገሩ፡ ባቲ፡ ወወሀቦሙ፡ መንፈሰ፡ ወ*ልሳነ፡ ወአፈ፡ ከመ፡ ይትናገሩ፡ ቦቱ።
source.note: Unapplied Charles1906 printed-edition scan candidate after an independent revise/hold pass; verify all glyphs and editor supplies afresh. No human or manuscript certification.

translation.text: And I lifted up my hands in righteousness and blessed the Holy and Great One. I spoke with the breath of my mouth[a] and with the tongue of flesh, which God made for the children of human flesh[b], so that they might speak with it. He gave them breath and tongue and mouth, so that they might speak with it.

footnotes.text: Or spirit of my mouth. Breath fits the immediate description of speech; the note does not change the printed Geʿez.
Literally children of the flesh of men; the bodily wording is retained.

source.text: ቡሩክ፡ አንተ፡ እግዚኦ፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ወኃያል፡ በዕበየ፡ ዚአከ፡ እግዚኦ፡ ኵሉ፡ ፍጥረት፡ ሰማይ፡ ንጉሠ፡ ነገሥት፡ ወአምላከ፡ ኵሉ፡ ዓለም፡ ወ*መላኵትከ፡ ወመንግሥትከ፡ ወዕበይከ፡ ይነብር፡ *ለዓለም፡ ወለዓለመ፡ ዓለም፡ ወለኵሉ፡ ትውልደ፡ ትውልድ፡ ስልጣንከ፡ ወኵሎሙ፡ ሰማያት፡ መንበርከ፡ ለዓለም፡ ወ*ኵላ፡ ምድር፡ መካይደ፡ እገሪከ፡ *ለዓለም፡ ወ*ለ*ዓለመ፡ ዓለም።

translation.text: Blessed are you, O Lord, great King and mighty in your greatness, Lord of all heavenly creation[a], King of kings and God of all the world. Your sovereign power[b], your kingdom, and your greatness endure forever and ever, and your authority endures through every generation. All the heavens are your throne forever, and the whole earth is the footstool of your feet forever and ever.[c]

footnotes.text: Literally all the creation of heaven; heavenly creation is a compact English rendering.
The printed royal-attribute noun is difficult, and sovereign power is provisional pending enlarged Charles glyph review; this is not an established your majesty reading.
Compare the throne-and-footstool imagery of Isaiah 66:1 without claiming identical wording.

source.text: እስመ፡ አንተ፡ ገበርከ፡ ወ*ለኵሉ፡ አንተ፡ ትመልክ፡ ወ*ኢይጸንዐከ፡ ግብር፡ *ወኢ፡ ፩[ወአሐቲ፡] ጥበብ፡ ኢትሐልፍ፡ *እምንባራተ፡ ምንባሪከ፡ ወኢትትመየጥ፡ ኢእምገጽከ፡ ወአንተ፡ ኵሎ፡ *ታአምር፡ ወትሬኢ፡ ወትሰምዕ፡ ወአልቦ፡ ዘይትኀባእ፡ እምኔከ፡ [እስመ፡ ኵሎ፡ ትሬኢ።]

translation.text: For you made all things, and you rule over everything. No deed is too hard for you—not even one.[a] Wisdom does not depart from the place of your throne or turn away from your presence.[b] You know and see and hear everything, and nothing is hidden from you.[c]

footnotes.text: Not even one concludes the statement about deeds. Charles brackets a following duplicated expression, and Wisdom begins a distinct personified statement.
This follows Charles’s reconstructed text. His printed p.162 notes 12–13 identify emendation and transposition, not an uncontested manuscript reading.

The concluding for you see all things is bracketed by Charles as a gloss in printed note 18; it is excluded from the running translation. The source vowel signs in the bracketed and throne phrases still need high-resolution review.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ *መላእክተ፡ ሰማያቲከ፡ ይኤብሱ፡ ወዲበ፡ ሥጋ፡ ሰብእ፡ ትከውን፡ መዐትከ፡ እስከ፡ ዕለት፡ ዐባይ፡ እንተ፡ ኵነኔ።
source.note: Unapplied Charles1906 printed-edition scan candidate after an independent revise/hold pass; verify all glyphs and editor supplies afresh. No human or manuscript certification.

translation.text: And now the angels of your heavens are guilty of sin, and your wrath will be upon human flesh[a] until the great day of judgment.

footnotes.text: Literally the flesh of men, referring collectively to mortal humanity; the printed main text names judgment directly.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ አምላክ፡ ወእግዚእ፡ ወንጉሥ፡ ዐቢይ፡ አስተበቍዕ፡ ወእስእል፡ ከመ፡ ታቅም፡ ሊተ፡ ስእለትየ፡ ከመ፡ ታተርፍ፡ ሊተ፡ ድኅረተ፡ ውስተ፡ ምድር፡ *ወኢታጥፍእ፡ ኵሎ፡ ሥጋ፡ ሰብእ፡ ወታዕርቃ፡ ለምድር፡ ወይከውን፡ ሐጕል፡ ለዓለም።
source.note: Unapplied Charles1906 printed-edition scan candidate after an independent revise/hold pass; verify all glyphs and editor supplies afresh. No human or manuscript certification.

translation.text: And now, O God and Lord and great King, I plead and ask that you grant my petition: preserve for me a remnant[a] on the earth, and do not destroy all human flesh and strip the earth bare, leaving it devastated forever.[b]

footnotes.text: Or posterity. The request concerns preserving human life and does not name particular survivors.

Do not destroy is explicit. The following earth-stripping and lasting-destruction clauses remain within that negative request. Charles printed p.163 note 6 reports variants in the earth-stripping clause, including negative forms.

source.text: ወይእዜኒ፡ እግዚእየ፡ አጥፍእ፡ *እምዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ሥጋ፡ እንተ፡ አምዐዐተከ፡ ወሥጋ፡ *ጽድቅ፡ ወርትዕ፡ አቅም፡ ለተክለ፡ ዘርእ፡ ለዓለም፡ ወኢትሰውር፡ ገጸከ፡ እምስእለተ፡ ገብርከ፡ እግዚኦ።
source.note: Unapplied Charles1906 printed-edition scan candidate after an independent revise/hold pass; verify all glyphs and editor supplies afresh. No human or manuscript certification.

translation.text: And now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh that provoked your wrath, but establish the flesh of righteousness and uprightness as a planting of seed forever.[a] Do not hide your face from the prayer of your servant, O Lord.[b]

footnotes.text: This ancient petition retains bodily and agricultural images, flesh and planting of seed. Forever is explicit in the source; it identifies no modern population and is not an instruction to readers.
The servant’s closing prayer remains in the selected printed text. Charles p.163 note 12 notes its omission in manuscript g; that omission has not silently replaced the main text.
